POLITICO: 'It's constant work': Mexico's new ambassador navigates a high-stakes moment with Washington
July 15, 2026 | 🟢

📰 A straight profile of new ambassador Roberto Lazzeri — and buried in it, the tell: Sheinbaum still hasn't spoken to Trump about the criminal complaints over Mexicans killed in ICE custody. 🇲🇽

Politico frames the USMCA review, extradition fights and ICE deaths as "high-stakes," and — rare for a US outlet — lets the Mexican envoy answer in his own words instead of a US official.

• Lazzeri on the job: "It's constant work"

AFP/YAHOO: Mexico City tourist area appears to come into cartel's crosshairs
July 17, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The headline puts Xochimilco "in a cartel's crosshairs." The article's own reporting: one unverified video, residents who call the canals peaceful, and police who report nothing. 🇲🇽

A masked man in a propaganda clip is not a cartel takeover — Mexico City has stayed largely untouched by the violence US and wire media keep forecasting for it.

• the masked gunman in the clip: "The clean-up has already begun"
• residents describe the neighborhood as "peaceful and with limited crime"

AP: Mexico asks US state attorneys general to investigate migrant ICE deaths
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AP's wire on the 17 Mexicans killed under Trump's crackdown cites the detention-center letters, the U.N. complaint, the diplomatic notes — and quotes exactly zero of the dead men or their families. 🇲🇽

Lorenzo Salgado Araujo — 52, no record, 35 years in the US — was shot by an ICE agent while driving his construction crew to work. That killing is why Mexico is now demanding criminal probes.

• "17 Mexican migrants have died… 14 in ICE custody and three in agency operations"
• "The United States is not legally obliged to act on the requests"

🇲🇽🛢️ WITH HORMUZ SHUT, MEXICO FUELS JAPAN

While the Strait of Hormuz stays shut, Mexico is keeping Japan's refineries fueled. One million barrels of Pemex crude reach Japan today — routed all the way around the Cape of Good Hope for Cosmo Oil, the first Mexican oil to land there since the US-Israel-Iran war erupted, El Financiero reports. Japan once drew over 90% of its oil from the Gulf; this shipment came straight out of a Sheinbaum–Takaichi call.

🔥🇲🇽 COCA-COLA WENT TO COURT TO KEEP JUNK FOOD IN SCHOOLS — AND LOST

Coca-Cola went to court to keep junk food in Mexican schools. It just lost — for now. The Supreme Court froze all 25 amparos filed against the ban on selling processed junk on campus, a corporate challenge led by the Coca-Cola system. Mexico's 2023 education law bars the sale and advertising of ultra-processed products in schools; the SCJN won't let lower courts gut it while it reviews.

🚨🇲🇽 BC GOVERNOR SAYS SHE WAS SET UP WITH FAKE 'US AGENTS'

Baja California's governor says she was set up. Marina del Pilar accuses her predecessor Jaime Bonilla of staging a meeting with fake "US agents" over her cancelled visa, to make it look like she was negotiating with Washington. "It was a montage — I was the victim of a deception and an act of political revenge," she said. Security chief García Harfuch confirmed no sensitive information was shared.

🔥🇲🇽 THE HUACHICOL EMPIRE HAD A JUDGE

Juan Pablo Gómez Fierro granted Ruffo's company Ingemar an amparo forcing the Energy Ministry to restore the fuel-import permit it had cancelled for irregularities. Contralínea reports Ingemar moved over 3 billion pesos at home and 1.38 billion dollars abroad — flows prosecutors call "incongruent with its fiscal profile."

🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM TO TRUMP: NO TO ICE TRAFFIC-STOP DETENTIONS

Trump ordered ICE to resume detaining migrants at traffic stops. Sheinbaum said no. "If a person must be deported under US law, then do it with respect for human rights," she answered, refusing to let irregular migration be treated as a crime — days after Mexico filed criminal complaints over the deaths of its nationals in ICE custody.

🚨🇲🇽 PAN ICON JAILED IN ALTIPLANO OVER MEXICO'S BIGGEST FUEL-SMUGGLING NETWORK

A PAN icon just landed in maximum security. Ernesto Ruffo — the party's first governor of Baja California — is in Altiplano, accused by the FGR of running the largest fuel-smuggling network ever detected in Mexico: Texas gasoline moved across the border by rail with only 10% of each tank car declared to customs. Prosecutor Ernestina Godoy puts the treasury damage at over 4 billion pesos.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICO'S MORTGAGE PORTFOLIO HITS RECORD 1.5 TRILLION PESOS

Mexico's mortgage credit balance reached 1.513 trillion pesos in May — a record since Banco de México began keeping the figure — up 20.6% in three years. Commercial banks project another 3–5% of growth through 2026, with delinquency at a healthy 3.11% and used homes now making up half of all purchases. The "two-speed economy" the financial press keeps predicting still hasn't shown up in the numbers. (El Economista)
